intro: A statistic changes from sample to sample. Pick a population, choose the sample size, and take samples: every sample's mean or proportion drops onto the bottom plot, and the sampling distribution builds dot by dot. Compare its center and spread with the formulas, and see when a normal model fits.
howItWorksTitle: How the samples are drawn and checked
howItWorks:
Each population is a histogram: its bars are the true proportions of the population in each interval, and a value is drawn by picking a bar with that chance and then a point at random inside it. So the population mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$ are exact. Samples are drawn independently (as from a very large population, so the 10% condition holds), from a seeded generator: the same seed gives the same samples.

The bottom plot shows every simulated statistic: dots while each fits, then a histogram. The formulas $\mu_{\bar{x}} = \mu$, $\sigma_{\bar{x}} = \sigma/\sqrt{n}$ and $\sigma_{\hat{p}} = \sqrt{p(1 - p)/n}$ are printed beside the simulated mean and standard deviation, and the normal curve, when shown, is that model drawn to the same scale. The shape rule is the AP® Statistics one: a normal population or $n \ge 30$ for $\bar{x}$, and $np \ge 10$ and $n(1 - p) \ge 10$ for $\hat{p}$.
